title: Momentum Gauge & Exit Checklist for Beta Launch
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, actionable tracker for the upcoming beta launch (small cohort -> open beta). Goal: provide a single-page Momentum Gauge that answers “are we building sustainable momentum?” and a compact Exit Checklist + contingency ladder for quick go/no-go decisions during the first 72 hours of ramp.

Audience:
- Product Ops (primary)
- PM + Eng leads for Hosted API and Dedicated features
- SRE on-call and Solutions Eng

High-level approach (why different):
- Focus on cohort-derived momentum (not only raw traffic). We care if early-adopter cohorts show retention and successful flows.
- Pair KPI thresholds with concrete ops actions (who does what when a threshold trips).
- Lightweight measurement so on-call can act without deep dashboards.

Quick summary (one-liner):
If 3 signal tiers (Green/Amber/Red) remain Green across behavioral (engagement), quality (error/latency), and economics (cost-per-call) for 48h -> proceed to staged ramp. Any Red in first 6h triggers immediate mitigation and potential rollback.

MOMENTUM GAUGE (single page)
- Time window: rolling 24h and 72h
- Cohorts: Early Integrations (E1: partners onboarded pre-launch), Internal QA, Open Beta signups (O1). Track separately and in aggregate.

Core signals and thresholds (operational thresholds — tweak for region/feature):
1) Engagement (behavioral)
  - Active sessions per cohort (24h): target E1 >= 30, O1 >= 200; amber if 60% of target; red if < 30% of target.
  - Successful request completion rate (end-to-end): green >= 98%, amber 95-98%, red <95%

2) Quality (service health)
  - 95th latency (generation endpoint): green <= 450ms, amber 450-800ms, red >800ms
  - Error rate (4xx+5xx per 1k requests): green <= 5, amber 6-20, red >20
  - Retries / fallback usage (automatic model fallback engaged): green <1%, amber 1-5%, red >5%

3) Economics (unit cost & quota health)
  - Cost per 1k tokens (estimated): green within budgeted CP1k, amber 1.2x, red >1.5x
  - Pool saturation (Dedicated): green <70%, amber 70-90%, red >90%

4) Product-level signals (user-visible)
  - Failed flows reported by beta users (tickets/week): green <=2, amber 3-7, red >=8
  - Qualitative NPS-like pulse (post-session survey): green >=4.0/5, amber 3.5-4.0, red <3.5

How to compute the Gauge (ops-friendly):
- For each category (Engagement, Quality, Economics, Product), compute a simple color by the worst-metric rule (if any metric is red, category=red).
- Momentum Gauge state = worst of the four categories.
- Keep a short rolling log (CSV or simple sheet rows) feeding the gauge for last 72h with timestamp, cohort, and state.

Owners and immediate actions (hands-on):
- On-call SRE (primary for Quality): triage within 15m of Red; follow SRE playbook for latency spikes (scale pools, flush caches, revert recent infra PRs).
- Product Ops (owner for Momentum Gauge): update stakeholders, run customer messaging if Product-level Red, coordinate throttles.
- Eng PM (hosted-api owner): approve traffic-shift decisions, coordinate canary rollbacks.
- Solutions Eng (partner-facing): open JIRA for partner issues, coordinate patch releases.

Exit Checklist (go/no-go decision logic for staged ramp)
- Minimum Green to proceed from Beta -> Gradual Ramp (48h window):
  1) Momentum Gauge = Green for both Early Integrations and Open Beta cohorts for 48h
  2) No new critical regressions (SEV2+) introduced in last 24h
  3) Observability: logs retained and traces sampled for 100% of beta traffic; alerts muting validated
  4) Support readiness: 2 available on-duty CS/SE reps for first 72h of ramp
  5) Capacity: Dedicated pool headroom >= 30% or hosted auto-burst validated

If any Exit criterion fails -> DELAY/REROUTE. Specific triggers: if Quality is Red for >6h -> rollback traffic to previous model variant and open incident.

Contingency ladder (fast actions):
- If Product Red only (user reports high but infra OK): throttle new signups, enable support chat priority, push quick fix (config/API param) with warm rollout.
- If Quality Amber -> scale dedicated pools + enable circuit-breaker (graceful degradation mode: shorter responses, lower-token cap) and re-evaluate after 30m.
- If Quality Red -> immediate rollback to prior model variant (or route to fallback region), page SRE, and pause marketing.
- If Economics Red -> enable cost-control mode (quantized responses, response token cap), switch traffic to cheaper model variant.

KPI Sheet (minimal, shareable) -> put into product-ops KPI tab but included here for reference:
Columns: metric | cohort | current_24h | target_24h | status | owner | action_if_trip
Examples (current numbers are placeholders — replace with live pulls):
- Active sessions | O1 | 217 | 200 | green | Maya Chen | NA
- Success rate (%) | E1 | 97.8 | 98.0 | amber | Liam O'Connor | Check model prompts + tokenization changes (PR#987)
- 95th latency (ms) | Overall | 512 | 450 | amber | SRE on-call | Scale pool + check kernel selection logs
- Error rate /1k | Overall | 4.2 | 5 | green | SRE on-call | monitor
- Cost per 1k tokens | Hosted | $3.10 | $2.80 | amber | Product Ops | enable cache & reduce batch size

Ops playbook snippets (copy these into runbooks):
- Latency spike immediate checklist (SRE): 1) Check pool saturation, 2) Check hot shards, 3) Increase instances or rotate to backup pool, 4) Capture pprof and flamegraphs, 5) Notify PM and Product Ops.
- Error rate spike (Engineering): 1) Identify top error codes via logs, 2) Reproduce with invocations from trace ids, 3) Roll back last deploy if correlated, 4) Hotfix patch route.

Communication protocol (short):
- Pager -> SRE primary (15m), Slack #launch-alerts -> everyone, Email -> exec summary if Red persists beyond 2h, Confluence incident page link in Slack thread.
- Product Ops to update the Momentum Gauge sheet every hour during launch hours (first 24h), then every 3h until 72h.

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- Confirm exact CP1k budget for APAC region (finance sign-off) — action: Ravi to confirm by 2026-03-05.
- Decide whether to expose a public status page toggle for early partners.
- Need a tiny consumer-friendly FAQ for partners if we throttle (Maya to draft).

Quick links and references:
- Launch spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Launch+Horizon
- On-call SRE runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbooks
- Partner list & contact sheet: drive:/shared_drives/customer-success/partner-rollout.csv
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/portal/pull/987

Final note (lean):
This doc should be operational, minimal, and copied into the product-ops KPI tab before final go/no-go. Keep the Gauge simple — if it’s hard to compute in 5 minutes, reduce metrics. We want confident decisions, not perfect telemetry.
